selection.text: Small delivery robots now share pavements with pedestrians
in several cities. They must recognise kerbs, crossings and
people from a single forward camera. Most of the software
runs on a low power board inside the robot body. This paper
describes the perception stack of one such robot and the tests
we ran on it.

script.text: Small delivery robots now share pavements with pedestrians in several cities.
They must recognise kerbs, crossings and people from a single forward camera.
Most of the software runs on a low power board inside the robot body.
This paper describes the perception stack of one such robot and the tests we ran on it.

selection.text: The stack has four stages that run once per camera frame. A
compact encoder turns each frame into a grid of features. The
planner then chooses a short path and sends wheel speeds to
the motors. Two helper processes watch the stack and restart
it when a stage stops responding.

selection.text: We drove the robot for three weeks on a university campus
with mixed foot traffic. Every run was recorded so that
failures could be replayed and analysed later. The robot
completed most deliveries without help from a remote
operator. Interventions happened mainly at crossings with
faded paint and at busy entrances.

script.text: We drove the robot for three weeks on a university campus with mixed foot traffic.
Every run was recorded so that failures could be replayed and analysed later.
The robot completed most deliveries without help from a remote operator.
Interventions happened mainly at crossings with faded paint and at busy entrances.

selection.text: The helper processes restarted a stalled stage nine times
during the trial. Each restart took less than two seconds and
the robot stopped safely while it waited. We now log the
memory use of every stage to find the cause of these stalls.
